JWT audience/lifetime/refresh-rotation - a property of the token issuer and resource-server config, not something a per-request tenant-isolation probe (deny/leak against a resource) can express.
Secrets hardcoded in application.yml - a static source finding with no HTTP request that could prove or disprove it.
Absence of rate limiting - not a tenant-isolation probe; proven by firing N requests and checking for a missing 429, unrelated to the deny/leak oracle this tool implements.
Absence of audit logging / tokens in plaintext logs - requires reading the application's own log stream and DB schema, not an API response, so it is out of this HTTP-only harness's reach.

SQL injection via the `sort` parameter (Injection category in SPEC.md section 2, not Tenant isolation) - the WHERE tenant_id=? filter stays parameterised, so there is no cross-tenant data returned for this harness's deny/leak oracle to catch. This harness deliberately never sends injection payloads. Manually/scanner-found instead (see targets/tenant-api/exploits/A-12-*.sh and scanners/).
SSRF via the webhook test endpoint - not a tenant-isolation probe (no cross-tenant actor/resource pair applies).
